privateLaunch: Run obdtrace app or open the private launch file shown in the terminal.
targetHint: Enter ble:NAME or ble:ID, or enter the outgoing serial port (serial:COM3). On Linux you can also enter a classic Bluetooth MAC address with the rfcomm: prefix.
noadapters: No adapters found. Follow the steps below.
clearq: Clear all trouble codes? This also erases freeze-frame data and resets readiness monitors. A backup log is saved first. Only do this after the codes have been read and the cause is dealt with.
save: Save the last minutes to a file
label: Label
nolive: Connect an adapter to see live data.
aiIntro: Connect your AI app to this program. The AI then reads the car through it.
aiNone: No AI client has connected yet.
aiClient: Which AI app do you use?
aiConfigured: Have you already added OBD2 to this AI app?
aiNew: No, help me set it up
vscodeReady: In VS Code, open the Command Palette, run MCP: List Servers, and start obd2 if it is not running. Use Copilot Chat to test.
claudeDesktopReady: Open Claude Desktop. If it is already open and you just saved the settings, restart it.
claudeCodeSetup: Run this command in a terminal, then open Claude Code in the same project.
testPrompt: Call the connection_status tool on the {{server}} MCP server.
configCopied: Configuration copied. Merge it into this file without removing existing servers:
prompts: What do you want to investigate?
promptsHint: Click, then paste into your AI chat.
reportHint: Creates local files. Review and redact them before sharing: masking the VIN does not make a report anonymous. Nothing is uploaded automatically.
safety: Safety: park the car. Do not read or clear codes while driving. Codes name a failed test, not a failed part.
adapterNote: Plug the adapter into the car's OBD-II port (under the dashboard) and switch the ignition on.
autoHistory: Every connected session is saved automatically. Ending an investigation does not stop session history.
copiedPrompt: Copied. Paste into your external AI. Nothing was sent automatically.
historyChanged: History updated. Refresh to see the latest saved assessments.
bt.windows.1: Open Settings → Bluetooth & devices and make sure Bluetooth is On.
bt.windows.2: Search for BLE adapters without pairing first. Pair in the OS if the adapter requires it. Unnamed BLE devices appear by ID.
bt.windows.3: Classic Bluetooth (SPP): pair the adapter using its documented PIN, then choose its outgoing COM port. Check Device Manager → Ports or Bluetooth → More Bluetooth settings → COM Ports.
bt.windows.4: If nothing is found: toggle Bluetooth off/on, unplug the adapter for 10 s, and check Settings → Privacy → Bluetooth allows desktop apps.
bt.macos.1: Open System Settings → Bluetooth and make sure it is On.
bt.macos.2: macOS asks “obdtrace / Terminal would like to use Bluetooth” the first time: click Allow. If you clicked Don't Allow: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Bluetooth → enable your terminal/app, then restart.
bt.macos.3: Search for BLE adapters first without pairing. Pair only if required by the adapter. Unnamed devices appear by ID.
bt.macos.4: Classic Bluetooth (SPP): pair in Bluetooth settings and use the outgoing serial:/dev/cu.… port if macOS exposes one. If it does not, use a BLE adapter.
bt.linux.1: Check the Bluetooth service: systemctl status bluetooth (start it with sudo systemctl enable --now bluetooth).
bt.linux.2: Unblock the radio: rfkill list, then rfkill unblock bluetooth.
bt.linux.3: Search for BLE adapters first without pairing. Allow access to BlueZ/D-Bus. Pair the device if the adapter requires it.
bt.linux.4: Classic Bluetooth (SPP): pair with bluetoothctl, then enter rfcomm:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF above. Channel 1 is the default; append @2 for channel 2, for example. An existing serial:/dev/rfcomm0 also works if you have permission to open it.
prompt.identify_symptom.title: Identify a symptom
prompt.explain_previous_fault.title: Explain the earlier fault
prompt.compare_after_clear.title: Compare after clearing
prompt.check_engine_light.title: Check engine light is on
prompt.check_engine_light.text: My check-engine light is on. Call connection_status, then read_dtcs if connected. Report which code categories and readiness data were read successfully. Use read_freeze_frame if needed and available; explain what it shows for its associated code without assuming the exact onset time. Explain the codes in plain language and suggest what to check before replacing parts.
prompt.rough_running.title: Engine runs rough or misfires
prompt.rough_running.text: The engine runs rough. Check connection_status and read_dtcs if connected. Use query_session on the automatic session for about a minute of existing idle data. Check rpm, engine_load, short_fuel_trim_b1, long_fuel_trim_b1, intake_manifold_pressure, maf and o2_b1s1_voltage as available. Assess RPM stability, fuel trims and MAP/MAF plausibility, and suggest what to test next.
prompt.fuel_economy.title: High fuel use or poor performance
prompt.fuel_economy.text: Fuel use is high or power is poor. Check connection_status and read_dtcs if connected, then use query_session for a short window of existing data. Evaluate coolant temperature, fuel trims and whether MAF is plausible for the recorded RPM and load. State which operating conditions the history covers and what cannot be inferred from those conditions.
prompt.inspection_ready.title: Before the inspection
prompt.inspection_ready.text: I am going to an emissions inspection. Check connection_status and use read_dtcs if connected. Report which supported monitors are incomplete and whether the ECU requests the warning light. Explain that this is not an inspection verdict and that clearing codes resets readiness.
prompt.intermittent.title: Fault only happens sometimes
prompt.intermittent.text: A fault appears only sometimes. Use the automatic session history; do not ask me to reproduce it. Establish the approximate occurrence time while parked, then use query_session and get_session_events over a bounded window. Compare with recorded normal operation under similar conditions and report any gaps.
prompt.used_car.title: Buying a used car
prompt.used_car.text: I am considering buying this used car. Check connection_status, then read_dtcs if connected. Check readiness and read distance_since_clear and run_time if available. Explain what might suggest recent clearing without treating engine run time as time since clearing. Say what to ask the seller or have inspected; this is not a full inspection.
prompt.overview.title: I do not know, give an overview
prompt.overview.text: Give me an OBD-II overview of this car. Use connection_status, then read_dtcs and get_live_snapshot if connected. Check per-sensor freshness and request only relevant stale or missing values with read_live_data. Summarise what looks normal, what looks odd and what was not measured.
prompt.safety: Use only OBD2 tools exposed by your MCP client; do not bypass missing tools. The car must be parked during interaction. Do not clear codes as a diagnostic step or request reproduction of a dangerous condition. A code names a failed test, not a failed part. Separate live, historical and simulated evidence, and say what is uncertain. Refer safety-critical issues to a qualified professional.
dtcCaution: The time a code was read is not necessarily when the fault began. A code identifies a failed test, not a failed part.
freezeNote: These are readings stored by the control module, not live values. Not every code has a freeze frame, and the exact time of the fault may be unknown.
clearComplete: The control module acknowledged the request to clear trouble codes.
reportBody:
**App:** v{{version}}

Describe the problem. Use simulated data if possible. Do not post private logs or vehicle identifiers.
